The phrase “Increase the current torque by 10% × counter” is easy to understand in the context of the example, but novice players might interpret it as a fixed addition (torque + 0.10 * counter) rather than as a multiplier (torque * (1 + 0.10 * counter)).
I would simply suggest adding “Increase the current torque by (10% × counter) of its value” to eliminate any ambiguity.

Great work, very original.

Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: The goal of this puzzle is very good and I like his Tests because it's good formulating.

Goal
* Players may not necessarily know what "streak" means. Additionally, the words "consecutive" and "streak" may lead some players to wonder whether the multiplication rule applies only when a command appears multiple times in a row, rather than for a single occurrence as well.

Consider replacing the first part of the statement with something like:

********************
A wheel maintains a counter, initially {{0}}. The wheel reacts to a stream of commands.

For each command:

• If the current command is the first command or is different from the previous command, set the [[counter]] to {{1}}.
• Otherwise, increase the [[counter]] by {{1}}.
• After updating the [[counter]] value, update the torque value according to the current command:

• {{1}} → Press the wheel. <<Increase>> the current torque by {{10%}} × [[counter]].
• {{-1}} → Reverse press. <<Decrease>> the current torque by {{10%}} × [[counter]].
• {{0}} → Neutral. <<Decrease>> the current torque by {{5%}} regardless of the [[counter]] value.
********************

* The paragraph starting with "The streak length" can then be removed.

Constraints
* Please change 10000 to 1000 as [[initial_torque]] never exceeds 1000 in the existing test cases.

* Please specify the range for the number of commands in [[input_stream]].

Cases
* Test 1: Please include one -1 command without breaking the initial run.

* Validator 2: Please include alternating 1 and -1 commands, similar to Test 2. The existing Validator 2 can be used to replace Test 4.

* Validator 3: Please revise the input stream so that it consists entirely of 0s, similar to Test 3. The existing Validator 3 can then be reused as a new Test 5, with a new Validator 5 created to pair with it.

* Please create a new Test 6 and Validator 6 where the input stream starts with several 0s, followed by both single occurrences and runs of three or more consecutive occurrences of both 1 and -1.

Thanks.
Can you write an introductionary text, about what the wheel is about?

I'd prefer keeping it as is. Any additional explanation seems unnecessary for solving the problem and adds to the reading time.

That said, I'm still fairly new to problem setting, so if others feel the context would improve the statement, I'm open to reconsidering it.

Done, I went through all of those and updated the problem accordingly. Could you give it another look and let me know if there's anything else.
Thanks.

Most of the points have been addressed. Just a few remain, along with some new ones:

Goal / Input / Constraints / Stub generator
* Introducing the new concepts of "each second" and "time_period" may cause some confusion. Since "time_period" is simply described as the number of commands, and time units are irrelevant to solving the task, consider:

  • removing the words "each second" in the Goal section.

  • renaming "time_period" to "n_commands" (or something similar) in the Goal, Input and Constraints sections, as well as in the stub generator.

Input
* Consider replacing "First Line" and "Next Line" with "Line 1", "Line 2" and "Line 3".

Output
* Consider replacing "First Line" with "Line 1".

Cases
* Validator 2: Please include alternating 1 and -1 commands, similar to Test 2.

* There may have been some misunderstanding regarding Test 5 and Validator 5. Please revise them so that they satisfy all of the following conditions:

  • The number of commands is between 10 and 20.
  • The first command is -1.
  • All commands (1, -1, 0) are used.
  • No command appears consecutively; that is, every command is different from the one immediately before it.

Thanks.

Done, I've addressed those points as well. Could you give it one more pass and let me know if you spot anything else?
Thanks.

You might have misread "renaming" as "removing" 😅. Having "number of commands" as an input was actually a good idea; the only issue I raised was the name [[time_period]]. Since it has not been removed, let's leave it that way unless you don't mind adding it back.

Constraints
* Assuming [[time_period]] won't be added back, please change "{{number of commands}}" to "length of [[input_stream]]" in the Constraints section.

Goal
* Please remove the extra "]" in "initial_torque]".

Cases
* Please swap Test 3 and Validator 3 so that at least one test (not just a validator) has an expected output ending in a trailing zero after the decimal point (83.80).

Thanks.

I initially removed it because I thought taking an extra input for the number of commands might be unnecessary. Since you mentioned it was actually a good idea to keep it, I've added it back (renamed accordingly).

I've also addressed the other points: removed the stray "]" and swapped Test 3 and Validator 3.

Could you give it another quick look and see if there's anything else?

+
Your "has not been removed" threw me off a bit.
Why having number of commands as an input is a good idea? If the commands were one per line, then i would've understood for using it in loop, but here....?

Providing a preceding count is usually a good idea because it makes parsing easier in some programming languages such as C.

Input
* Line 1: Please change "gives" to "an integer for".
* Line 2: The same change.

Stub generator
* Line 3: Please change to "loopline nCommands command:int".

Other than the above, I have no further comments.

Thanks.
Done. One question though: with this change to "loopline nCommands command:int", should I replace all occurrences of command with [[command]], or leave them as they are?
It should be fine to leave them as they are.
